purpose: Preserve separation between capability, possession, delegation, and current execution authority.
Require contemporaneous transition admission independently of prior authorization.
Bind execution to an admitted consequential transition and preserve execution-boundary control.
Distinguish no effect, partial effect, completed effect, compensation, and reversal.
Keep execution, settlement progression, reconciliation, and finality independently represented.
Govern compensation as a new financially consequential execution rather than implicit rollback.
Govern reversal as a distinct consequential execution while preserving original history.
Separate reconciliation, reconstruction, economic equivalence, and restoration.
Require persistent evidence for execution, refusal, effect, remediation, classification, and historical lineage.
Separate settlement finality from authorization, legitimacy, continuity, and historical integrity.
Preserve distinction between continuous integrity, reconstruction, restored function, and reconciled history.
Prevent consensus or replicated agreement from becoming implicit financial authority.
Require current jurisdictional applicability and prevent authority expansion across governance boundaries.
Bind autonomous financial execution to a valid principal, delegation, scope, and current authority.
